comments.note: personas/node_modules/@mistralys/persona-builder was at 2.3.0 while package-lock.json referenced 2.4.0. A prior WP (WP-004) updated the lock file but did not run `npm install` to materialize the upgrade. This silent discrepancy meant deep-agents output was silently skipped without any build error. Consider adding a node_modules version validation step to the build script, or adding `npm install` to the build-personas.js preamble when a version mismatch is detected.

The build script's pre-clean loop (which deletes all .md files from output dirs before building) correctly covered outputDirs entries — no stale files were left. This was observed working correctly for the deep-agents directories.

comments.note: The cross-reference check in scripts/build-personas.js (WP-007) is scoped only to personas/ledger/src/meta. Standalone personas do not use {{agent_slug_*}} variables, which is correct — but worth documenting explicitly so a future maintainer doesn't inadvertently introduce slug variables in standalone templates without wiring up the check.

The validator emits a [WARN] for 'Unresolved variable' from persona-builder itself, plus a separate [ERROR] from the cross-reference check. These are two independent failure signals for the same root cause. Consider consolidating these messages to avoid confusion in CI logs.

No unit tests exist specifically for the cross-reference check logic (extractSubagentsList, etc.) in build-personas.js. The manual --check flag covers integration, but an isolated unit test for the parser would guard against future regressions in the YAML parsing logic.

summary: WP-008 is a build-and-verify task. The sole code change (running npm install to materialize the v2.4.0 upgrade from the already-updated lock file) is correct and sufficient.

The cross-reference check logic in scripts/build-personas.js (added by WP-007) is well-implemented: extractSubagentsList handles inline comment stripping, empty multiline guards, and stops at the next top-level YAML key cleanly. The {{agent_slug_*}} regex and slug normalisation (_→-) are correct.
parseYamlScalars trailing-comment limitation is explicitly documented as a convention constraint — no inline comments on scalar fields. Adequate for the use case.
Clean pre-build deletion loop correctly covers the new deep-agents output directories via the outputDirs config key. No stale files observed.
All 4 ACs confirmed passing by QA; 1826/1826 MCP server tests pass. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: extractSubagentsList (scripts/build-personas.js) uses ' #' (space+hash) to strip inline YAML comments on list items. A value like `slug#comment` (no leading space) would not be stripped. Given the persona YAML style, this edge case is practically unreachable, but worth noting for future YAML parsers.

[documentation-forward] WP-008.md spec file lists WP-005 as a dependency, but the ledger registered WP-003 instead. The spec file should be corrected to reflect the actual dependency graph (WP-003, WP-004, WP-007) so it does not mislead future readers tracing the execution order.

[documentation-forward] scripts/build-personas.js performs the {{agent_slug_*}} cross-reference check only against personas/ledger/src/meta. There is no comment explaining that standalone personas intentionally do not use agent_slug variables. An inline comment at the metaFiles scan point would prevent a future maintainer from wondering if standalone personas were accidentally excluded.
